target.title: feat: add maref-governance extension for AI agent safety enforcement
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Multi-agent AI systems need real-time guardrails to prevent unsafe file writes and command execution. Without a governance layer, any agent can modify sensitive files or execute arbitrary commands — creating security risks in collaborative AI workflows. This extension provides a pluggable, fail-closed enforcement layer via an external MAREF sidecar.

## Summary

Adds the **MAREF Governance** extension — a pluggable AI agent safety enforcement layer that intercepts file writes and command execution to validate them against an external MAREF sidecar.

## Key Features

- **before_tool_call hook**: Intercepts `write` and `exec` tool calls before they execute
- **Three enforcement modes**:
  - `enforcing` (default): Blocks operations that violate policy
  - `advisory`: Logs warnings but never blocks — for gradual rollout
  - `logging`: Bypasses sidecar checks entirely — zero overhead
- **Fail-closed**: When the sidecar is unreachable in enforcing mode, operations are blocked by default
- **HITL support**: Operations flagged as `hitl_required` are blocked with a message asking for human operator intervention
- **Security audit collector**: Reports governance status from the sidecar into OpenClaw's audit framework
- **Configurable**: sidecar URL, enforcement mode, fail-closed toggle

## Implementation Details

- Uses `definePluginEntry` from `openclaw/plugin-sdk/plugin-entry`
- Communicates with MAREF sidecar via `@maref-org/sdk` client
- Registers a `before_tool_call` hook and a `securityAuditCollector`
- 19 unit tests covering all enforcement modes, fail-closed behavior, sidecar errors, and audit collector

## Configuration

```json
{
  "sidecarUrl": "http://localhost:8000",
  "mode": "enforcing",
  "failClosed": true
}
```

## Dependencies

- `@maref-org/sdk@^0.2.0` (published on npm)

## Testing Evidence

```bash
# All 19 tests pass locally:
$ pnpm vitest run extensions/maref-governance
✓ 19 tests passed
```

target.title: fix(signal): preserve reverse-proxy path prefixes
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where users running the native Signal channel behind a reverse proxy path prefix, such as `http://127.0.0.1:8080/signal`, would still send RPC, health-check, and SSE requests to the origin root (`/api/v1/...`) instead of the configured prefix (`/signal/api/v1/...`).

That can make Signal send/check/receive flows fail with 404s even though `channels.signal.httpUrl` points at the correct mounted Signal service.

## Why This Change Was Made

`resolveSignalEndpointUrl` now keeps the parsed base URL pathname before appending the Signal native endpoint suffix. Root-mounted base URLs keep the existing `/api/v1/...` behavior, while path-prefixed base URLs now resolve beneath the configured prefix.

The change is limited to the native Signal client URL join helper. Container-mode Signal URL construction is separate and already preserves its configured path prefix, so it is intentionally unchanged.

## User Impact

Operators can run the native Signal HTTP/SSE API behind a path-prefixed reverse proxy and use the same configured `httpUrl` for sends, health checks, and event streaming.

## Evidence

### Live reverse-proxy behavior proof

I ran the current PR head against a local path-prefixed reverse-proxy setup:

```text
OpenClaw Signal native client
-> http://127.0.0.1:<proxy-port>/signal
-> path-prefixed reverse proxy
-> native-compatible signal-cli JSON-RPC/SSE service
```

This proof does not use a private Signal account or credentials. It validates the deployment behavior changed by this PR: the native OpenClaw Signal client preserves the configured `httpUrl` pathname before sending RPC, health-check, and SSE requests.

```text
[proof topology] OpenClaw Signal native client -> path-prefixed reverse proxy -> native-compatible signal-cli JSON-RPC/SSE service
[proof baseUrl] http://127.0.0.1:63713/signal
[before-current-main-shape] new URL('/api/v1/check', baseUrl).pathname=/api/v1/check -> HTTP 404
[openclaw] signalCheck(baseUrl) -> ok=true status=204
[openclaw] signalRpcRequest('version') -> {version:proof-signal-native}
[openclaw] streamSignalEvents(account=<redacted-e164>) -> [{event:message,data:{"source":"reverse-proxy-proof"},id:proof-1}]
[proxy] GET /api/v1/check rejected outside /signal mount -> 404
[proxy] GET /signal/api/v1/check -> 204
[proxy] POST /signal/api/v1/rpc -> 200
[proxy] GET /signal/api/v1/events?account=<redacted-e164> -> 200
[mock-native-signal] GET /api/v1/check -> 204
[mock-native-signal] POST /api/v1/rpc method=version -> 200
[mock-native-signal] GET /api/v1/events?account=<redacted-e164> accept=text/event-stream -> 200
```

### Focused tests

Focused behavior covered in tests:

- RPC request: `http://server/signal/` resolves to `/signal/api/v1/rpc`.
- Health check: `http://server/signal` resolves to `/signal/api/v1/check`.
- SSE receive stream: `http://server/signal` resolves to `/signal/api/v1/events?account=...`.

Closes #106910

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where installed `AgentToolResultMiddleware` handlers on the
OpenClaw embedded runtime never received `agentId`, `sessionId`,
`sessionKey`, or `runId`, even though those fields are part of the public
middleware context and the Codex path already forwards them. Middleware
used for audit, telemetry, or session-scoped policy therefore could not
attribute OpenClaw tool-result events.

## Why This Change Was Made

`buildAgentToolResultMiddlewareFactory` constructed
`createAgentToolResultMiddlewareRunner({ runtime: "openclaw" })` only.
Pass agent/session/run identity from the embedded attempt (and compact)
call sites into that runner, matching the Codex `toToolResultHookContext`
shape. Fall back to `SessionManager.getSessionId()` when an explicit
session id is not provided.

## User Impact

Installed middleware that declares OpenClaw runtime support can now see
the same agent/session/run identity fields on OpenClaw tool results that
it already receives on Codex.

## Evidence

```console
AFTER  {"runtime":"openclaw","agentId":"main","sessionId":"s-explicit","sessionKey":"agent:main:chat","runId":"run-1"}
```

target.title: feat(ui): custom session icons with agent-drawable SVG and nav-parity pinned rows
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Pinned sessions promote a conversation into the sidebar's quick-access zone, but they still read like list rows: no icon, session-row typography, a relative-time meta. They should feel like first-class sidebar entries — visually identical to the nav pages (Usage, Automations, Plugins) — and be personalizable: users pick a cute icon from the session menu, and agents can set one too, including drawing a tiny SVG themselves.

## Why This Change Was Made

- **Icon model**: sessions get an optional `icon` string — a single emoji grapheme, `name:<id>` resolved against a curated UI registry (12 icons), or `svg:<svg …>` sanitized server-side. The shared parser/sanitizer lives in `packages/gateway-protocol/src/session-icon.ts`; the sanitizer is a strict hand-written tokenizer (fail closed: whitelisted elements/attributes only, no scripts/handlers/hrefs/url()/data:/DOCTYPE/comments/namespaces, paint values restricted, ≤4 KB, canonical reserialization). The UI re-validates before rendering SVG via `unsafeHTML`.
- **Protocol**: additive `icon` on `sessions.patch` (null clears) and on session rows/events. Write scope matches the other chat-organization fields (operator.write). No version bump.
- **Agent surface**: the `sessions` tool's `patch` action gains `icon`, so an agent can pick a curated icon, an emoji, or draw its own SVG.
- **Persistence**: `icon` rides the session store entry next to `pinnedAt` and survives list projection, realtime `sessions.changed` events, session reset, and compaction checkpointing. `name:*` ids resolve via own-property lookup (a `name:constructor` icon falls back to the default instead of walking the prototype).
- **Pinned-row parity**: pinned rows now render a 16 px icon slot plus nav-item metrics/colors (32 px min-height, 8 px gap, 13 px/500 text, same hover/active fills) and drop the relative-time meta; unread dot, run spinner, child terminal badges, and the hover pin/menu actions stay.
- **Picker**: the session "…" menu gains "Change icon" — an arrow-key-navigable grid of the curated set, a custom-emoji input, and Remove icon.

## User Impact

Pinned sessions look and feel like sidebar pages, each with its own icon. Users set icons from the session menu; agents can set or draw them via the `sessions` tool.

Before | After | Picker
--- | --- | ---
![before](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/steipete/openclaw-pr-assets/main/sidebar-pinned-headerless/after.png) | ![after](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/steipete/openclaw-pr-assets/main/sidebar-session-icons/icons-after.png) | ![picker](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/steipete/openclaw-pr-assets/main/sidebar-session-icons/icons-after-picker.png)

## Evidence

- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs packages/gateway-protocol/src/session-icon.test.ts src/gateway/sessions-patch.test.ts src/agents/tools/sessions-tool.test.ts` — 11 + 86 + 10 passed (hostile-SVG rejection matrix: script/onload/xlink/url()/DOCTYPE/oversized/double-root).
- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs ui/src/components/app-sidebar.test.ts ui/src/components/session-menu.test.ts ui/src/lib/sessions/reconcile.test.ts` — green, including new cases: pinned emoji/named render, unknown-name + `name:constructor` fallback, picker patches `sessions.patch`.

target.title: fix(codex): stop stale MCP child processes with revalidated SIGKILL escalation
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

`killStaleComputerUseMcpChildren` in `extensions/codex/src/app-server/computer-use.ts:1146` sends `process.kill(pid, "SIGTERM")` and immediately records the pid as killed — without verifying the process actually terminated. If a child process traps or ignores SIGTERM (e.g. `process.on('SIGTERM', ...)` without `process.exit()`), it survives and becomes a zombie that the periodic health monitor can never clear.

## Why This Change Was Made

The fix schedules a SIGKILL after a 2-second grace period. Before sending SIGKILL, it **revalidates process identity** using three checks:
1. **PID existence**: `process.kill(pid, 0)` — quick liveness probe
2. **Immutable launch identity**: `lstart` (process start time) from `/bin/ps` — a PID reused by another matching MCP child within the grace period has a different start time, so the SIGKILL is correctly aborted even when command and ancestry match
3. **Command class + ancestry**: re-confirms the PID is still a `SkyComputerUseClient` MCP child descendant of the original ancestor PID

The timer is `unref()`'d so it does not keep the event loop alive. The kill path is macOS-gated (`process.platform !== "darwin"` early return) — no change to the platform guard.

The function returns `killedPids` immediately after SIGTERM (current contract), while the SIGKILL escalation is asynchronous. This is intentional: the repair reports what was terminated on the best-effort SIGTERM path, and the async SIGKILL handles the remaining misbehaving children silently.

Collision check: searched open PRs for `killStaleComputerUseMcpChildren`, `SIGKILL`, `lstart`, `computer-use`; no same-file or same-problem open PR was found.

## User Impact

Codex app-server health monitor now reliably terminates stale Computer Use MCP child processes, even those that ignore SIGTERM. PID reuse is guarded by immutable launch identity (`lstart`) comparison — a replacement MCP child with the same command and ancestry will not be mistakenly killed.

## Evidence

Exact head: `14f57eb24a75c4af90fe6534d7af91da8579523f`

### Format and diff check

```
$ git diff --check origin/main..HEAD && echo ok
ok
```

### Vitest suite

```
$ node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/codex/src/app-server/computer-use.test.ts

 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  37 passed (37)
```

Tests cover:
- SIGTERM is sent to identified stale MCP children
- After 2s grace period, revalidation confirms identity (PID + lstart + command + ancestry) → SIGKILL sent
- After 2s, quick existence check (`kill 0`) throws ESRCH → SIGKILL skipped
- After 2s, revalidation ps shows different command → SIGKILL skipped
- After 2s, revalidation ps shows same command but different lstart → SIGKILL skipped (PID reuse guard)

### Real behavior proof — production function verified on real processes

The proof script overrides `process.platform` to `"darwin"` and imports `killStaleComputerUseMcpChildren` directly from the production module. It spawns real child processes matching the `SkyComputerUseClient mcp` pattern, then calls the production function to verify the full SIGTERM → revalidate → SIGKILL lifecycle on real Linux processes. POSIX signal behavior and `/bin/ps lstart` are identical across Darwin and Linux.


target.title: fix(secrets): collect persona-level TTS provider SecretRefs
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Persona-level TTS provider API keys were not collected as SecretRefs and agent persona registry paths bound the wrong path segment as providerId (literal `providers` instead of `elevenlabs`). That breaks secrets plan/audit and runtime resolution for agent persona TTS keys.

Fixes #89607

## Summary

The secret collector walks `messages.tts.providers.*.apiKey` but does not walk `messages.tts.personas.*.providers.*.apiKey` or `agents.list[].tts.personas.*.providers.*.apiKey`. When a persona overrides the TTS provider config with a file-source SecretRef, the secret resolver never sees the ref, so the `apiKey` reaches the plugin as an unresolved object instead of the actual key string. The plugin then reports `not configured`.

This fix:
- Adds persona-level provider iteration in `collectTtsApiKeyAssignments`
- Registers two new target paths in the secret target registry (`messages.tts.personas.*.providers.*.apiKey` and `agents.list[].tts.personas.*.providers.*.apiKey`)
- Extends `hasAgentRuntimeSecretRefs` to detect persona-level TTS refs
- Adds 5 regression tests covering top-level, persona-level, combined, empty-persona, and agent-level persona paths

Closes #89607

## Evidence

Terminal output from `tsx` against the patched branch showing correct `providerId` binding and persona file SecretRef collection (see Real behavior proof for full capture).

## Real behavior proof

- **Behavior or issue addressed:** Agent persona TTS SecretRef paths must resolve `providerId` to the provider key (e.g. `elevenlabs`), not the literal `providers` segment, so plan/audit/runtime metadata match the configured provider. Persona-level file SecretRefs must be collected under `agents.list[].tts.personas.*.providers.*.apiKey`.
- **Real environment tested:** macOS arm64, Node v22, OpenClaw branch `fix/tts-persona-secretref` at `/tmp/oc-89636`, commit after providerId index fix.
- **Exact steps or command run after this patch:**

  ```bash
  cd /tmp/oc-89636
  pnpm exec vitest run src/secrets/target-registry.test.ts src/secrets/runtime-config-collectors-tts.test.ts
  pnpm exec tsx /tmp/proof-tts-providerid.mjs
  pnpm exec tsx /tmp/proof-tts-collect.mjs
  ```

- **Evidence after fix:** terminal output from the patched source:

  ```console
  ✓ src/secrets/target-registry.test.ts (10 tests)
  ✓ src/secrets/runtime-config-collectors-tts.test.ts (5 tests)
  Test Files  2 passed (2)

  {"path":"agents.list.0.tts.providers.elevenlabs.apiKey","entryId":"agents.list[].tts.providers.*.apiKey","providerId":"elevenlabs"}
  ```

target.title: fix(scripts): preserve surrogate pairs when truncating LLM text in bench dump
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

`scripts/repro/tool-surface-live-bench.ts` uses `String.prototype.slice(0, N)` at three sites to truncate LLM output text for benchmark trail/log output. `slice` operates on UTF-16 code units, so when a surrogate pair (emoji, CJK character) straddles the cut boundary at position 299-300 or 399-400, the result contains an unpaired high surrogate — invalid Unicode that downstream consumers may reject.

## Why This Change Was Made

Replace with `truncateUtf16Safe` from `@openclaw/normalization-core/utf16-slice`, the same helper already used across the codebase for safe UTF-16 boundary truncation. Sibling UTF-16 PRs (#104054, #107664, #109561, #109498, #109839) all use the same helper. The 300- and 400-code-unit limits and all non-truncated output remain unchanged.

Collision check: no open same-file or same-problem PR was found.

## User Impact

Benchmark trail and result dump output no longer produces invalid Unicode. No production impact — this file is a `scripts/repro/` bench tool.

## Evidence

### Format and diff check

```
$ git diff --check origin/main..HEAD && echo ok
ok
```

### Focused test suite

```
$ node scripts/run-vitest.mjs test/scripts/tool-surface-live-bench.test.ts
 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  8 passed (8)
```

### Real behavior proof — bench run against mock OAI Responses endpoint

A loopback mock HTTP server on 127.0.0.1:19876 returns OAI Responses API SSE with boundary-straddling text (🐱 at UTF-16 positions [299,300] and [399,400]). The bench is invoked with `BENCH_DUMP=1` and `--providers=openai --surfaces=direct --tasks=top-plot`. This exercises the exact production code path through the Agent → model fetch → stream processing → trail dump pipeline.

**Before fix** (raw `.slice(0, N)`) — the ASSISTANT trail text ends with U+FFFD (terminal rendering of unpaired surrogate), and the result JSON `finalText` field contains a trailing `\ud83d` (unpaired high surrogate):

```
===== DUMP openai/direct/top-plot ok=false =====
ASSISTANT text: xxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxx...xxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxx�
===== END DUMP =====
... "finalText": "...xxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxx🐱yyyyyyyyyyyyyyyyyyyyyyyyyyyyyyyyyyyyyyyyyyyyyy\ud83d"
```

**After fix** (`truncateUtf16Safe`) — the ASSISTANT trail text is clean (299 chars, surrogate pair dropped at boundary), and `finalText` has no trailing surrogate (399 chars, first 🐱 preserved intact, second 🐱 at 399-400 dropped correctly):

```
===== DUMP openai/direct/top-plot ok=false =====
ASSISTANT text: xxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxx...xxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxx
===== END DUMP =====
... "finalText": "...xxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxx🐱yyyyyyyyyyyyyyyyyyyyyyyyyyyyyyyyyyyyyyyyyyyyyy"
```

Site-by-site analysis at this exact head (6a23f108ec5c):
- **site1** (ASSISTANT text, 300-unit boundary): `truncateUtf16Safe` returns 299 code units, no trailing surrogate. Raw `.slice(0,300)` retains U+D83D at position 299.
- **site2** (TOOLRESULT, 400-unit boundary): same helper, same boundary logic; covered by the 8 unit tests validating the 400-unit path.
- **site3** (finalText, 400-unit boundary): `truncateUtf16Safe` returns 399 code units with the first 🐱 intact, no trailing surrogate. Raw `.slice(0,400)` retains U+D83D at position 399.

### Not tested

- Live multi-provider LLM bench against real OpenAI/Anthropic/Google endpoints (requires production API keys)
- TOOLRESULT truncation site with boundary-straddling tool output (the identically-named call path uses `truncateUtf16Safe` with the same limit and is covered by the unit tests)

`setTtsMaxLength` accepts any number value without validation. Negative, NaN, Infinity, or zero values can be persisted to disk, causing downstream TTS failures when these invalid values are used as speech length limits.

## User Impact

Invalid maxLength values are rejected at the API boundary with a descriptive RangeError, preventing silent misconfiguration of TTS speech length limits.

- [x] This change has been tested with existing configurations

target.title: fix(test-performance-agent): hang up to 240m when a git fetch stalls
target.body:
<!--
Optional linked context:
Add a visible `Closes #<issue-number>` or `Related: #<issue-number>` line
below this comment.

Required PR title:
type: user-facing description
Use a parenthesized scope only when it adds clarity:
fix(auth): login redirect loops when session cookie is expired

Types: feat, fix, improve, refactor, docs, chore.
For fixes, describe the user-visible symptom and trigger:
fix: task list fails to load when user has no environments
Avoid implementation details such as:
fix: add null check to task query
-->

Related: #110279, #110281, #110028, #110282, #109176 (recent `git fetch` timeout-bounding pattern in other workflows).

<details>
<summary>Additional instructions</summary>

**MUST:** Keep **Allow edits from maintainers** enabled for this PR so maintainers
can help update the branch when needed.

</details>

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where the `Test Performance Agent` workflow (`.github/workflows/test-performance-agent.yml`) could hang for the full 240-minute job ceiling when a `git fetch` stalled. The workflow had two unbounded `git fetch --no-tags origin ...` calls — one in the `Gate trusted main activity and daily cadence` step that checks whether the CI run was superseded, and one in the `Commit test performance updates` step that refreshes the target branch before pushing the optimized test commit. Neither had a per-command kill, so a stalled network fetch would block the daily run until the job-level `timeout-minutes: 240` expired.

## Why This Change Was Made

Both `git fetch` calls are now prefixed with `timeout --signal=TERM --kill-after=10s 120s`, matching the established pattern already used across the repo in `ci.yml` (preflight, base-SHA and QA profile selected-ref fetches) and `qa-profile-evidence.yml`.

- On a normal fetch that completes within 120s, `timeout` passes through exit 0 and stdout unchanged, so the existing 5-attempt retry loops behave exactly as before.
- On a stalled fetch, `timeout` sends TERM after 120s (exit 124) and force-kills after a further 10s if the process ignores TERM; the existing retry loop then continues to the next attempt, preserving current retry semantics.

A focused regression test (`bounds test-performance-agent git fetch operations`) was added to `test/scripts/ci-workflow-guards.test.ts`, mirroring the existing `bounds QA profile selected-ref fetches` guard. Non-goals: no retry-count, sleep-backoff, push, or rebase logic was touched, and no secrets, schema, config, or API boundaries changed.

## User Impact

CI operators and contributors relying on the daily Test Performance Agent run no longer risk a single stalled `git fetch` consuming the full 240-minute job budget. A hung fetch now fails fast (within ~2 minutes) and lets the workflow's existing retry/recovery logic proceed, keeping the daily test-performance optimization cadence healthy.

## Evidence

**Focused regression (red → green):**

- `bounds test-performance-agent git fetch operations` fails on the unmodified workflow (no `timeout` prefix on either `git fetch` line) and passes after the fix.

```
$ pnpm exec vitest run test/scripts/ci-workflow-guards.test.ts -t "bounds test-performance-agent git fetch operations"
 ✓ tooling  ../scripts/ci-workflow-guards.test.ts (86 tests | 85 skipped) 28ms
 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  1 passed | 85 skipped (86)
```

Red confirmation (workflow reverted to unbounded `git fetch`, test run): the same assertion fails at `gitFetchLines.every(...).toBe(true)` because neither `git fetch` line contains the `timeout --signal=TERM --kill-after=10s 120s` prefix.

**Repo-wide format check:** `pnpm format:check` reports `All matched files use the correct format.`

**Scope:** only `.github/workflows/test-performance-agent.yml` (lines 61 and 247) and `test/scripts/ci-workflow-guards.test.ts` (one new `it` block) are changed.

target.title: fix(browser): honor abort signal during CDP handshake retry backoff
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

`withCdpSocket` in `extensions/browser/src/browser/cdp.helpers.ts` retries failed WebSocket handshakes on a 200ms→3s exponential backoff (with jitter, up to 2 extra attempts) using an unabortable `sleep`. The browser permissions route (`routes/permissions.ts`) already receives the per-request `AbortSignal` and calls `params.signal.throwIfAborted()` around every other stage of `grantPermissions` — but the `withCdpSocket` call passed only `commandTimeoutMs`, so an aborted permission grant still waited out the remaining handshake backoff before the abort was noticed.

## Why This Change Was Made

`CdpSocketOptions` gains an optional `signal`, the backoff sleep uses `sleepWithAbort(ms, opts?.signal)` from `openclaw/plugin-sdk/runtime-env` (the same helper and import path as the merged #109710 Playwright-click and #109617 tab-discovery browser fixes), and the permissions route passes its `params.signal` through. An abort landing mid-backoff now rejects the sleep with the stable `Error("aborted")` from `sleepWithAbort`, which propagates out of `withCdpSocket` before any further socket is opened. Callers that pass no signal see zero behavior change — `sleepWithAbort(ms, undefined)` degenerates to the plain timer, and already-aborted signals are handled by the helper itself.

## Changes

- Thread an optional `signal` through `CdpSocketOptions`; handshake retry backoff sleeps via `sleepWithAbort`.
- Pass the request `signal` at the `grantPermissions` CDP call site.
- Regression test in `cdp.helpers.internal.test.ts`: a real `ws` `WebSocketServer` on 127.0.0.1 always rejects handshakes with 503; `withCdpSocket` runs with `handshakeRetries: 5` and a 30s retry delay; abort fires once the first rejection lands inside the backoff. Asserts rejection with `/aborted/`, wall clock under 10s, and exactly one handshake attempt (no second socket).

## User Impact

Cancelling a browser permission request (or its page/route operation timing out) while Chrome is unreachable no longer lingers through the remaining handshake retry backoff; the route tears down promptly instead of opening doomed sockets.

## Evidence

Exact head: `35432ce27de1131cccb352e8a82e099b191064dc`.

**Outside-runner behavior proof** — the production `withCdpSocket` is driven directly (no test runner, no mocks) via `node --import tsx` against a real loopback `ws` WebSocket server whose `verifyClient` rejects every handshake with 503 and counts attempts. The abort fires the moment the first rejected handshake lands inside the 3000ms backoff.

After fix — abort mid-backoff rejects in 1ms with the abort reason, exactly one handshake attempt, no second socket:

```text
$ TSX_TSCONFIG_PATH=tsconfig.json node --import tsx /tmp/cdp-abort-proof.mts; echo "EXIT=$?"
[proof] loopback CDP WebSocket server: ws://127.0.0.1:40533/devtools/browser/TEST
[proof-server] handshake attempt #1 rejected with 503
[proof] AbortController.abort() fired at +29ms (inside 3000ms backoff)
[proof] outcome expect=after settled=rejected elapsedMs=30 abortAtMs=29 abortToRejectMs=1 handshakeAttempts=1 error="aborted"
[proof] check ok: withCdpSocket rejects (handshake never succeeds)
[proof] check ok: after-fix: rejection is the abort reason ("aborted")
[proof] check ok: after-fix: abort-to-reject 1ms < 1000ms (backoff was 3000ms)
[proof] check ok: after-fix: exactly one handshake attempt, no retry after abort (got 1)
[proof] OK
EXIT=0
```

Before fix (same script with `extensions/browser/src/browser/cdp.helpers.ts` from `upstream/main`, restored immediately after): the abort at +12ms is ignored, handshake attempts #2 and #3 still fire on the full 3000ms schedule, and the rejection arrives 6135ms after the abort with the retry-exhaustion error instead of the abort reason.

```text
[proof-server] handshake attempt #1 rejected with 503
[proof] AbortController.abort() fired at +12ms (inside 3000ms backoff)
[proof-server] handshake attempt #2 rejected with 503
[proof-server] handshake attempt #3 rejected with 503
[proof] outcome expect=before settled=rejected elapsedMs=6147 abortAtMs=12 abortToRejectMs=6135 handshakeAttempts=3 error="Unexpected server response: 503"
[proof] check ok: before-fix: rejection is the retry-exhaustion failure, not the abort ("Unexpected server response: 503")
[proof] check ok: before-fix: abort ignored until backoff elapsed (6147ms >= 3000ms)
[proof] check ok: before-fix: retry fired despite the abort (attempts=3)
[proof] OK (expect=before)
```

Regression tests:

```text
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run extensions/browser/src/browser/cdp.helpers.internal.test.ts
Test Files  1 passed (1)
Tests  29 passed (29)
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run extensions/browser/src/browser/routes/permissions.test.ts
Test Files  1 passed (1)
```

Same new test against the pre-change implementation (file at `upstream/main`): the abort is ignored, the loop rides out the 30s backoff per attempt, and the run stalls until the 120s Vitest watchdog terminates it — the fixed implementation passes the same test in under 1s against a real loopback WebSocket server (no mocked fetch).

`oxlint` clean on all three changed files; `tsgo` extensions project reports no errors in browser files.

## Intentionally out of scope

- The other `withCdpSocket` call sites (`chrome.ts`, `cdp-page-session.ts`, `chrome.graphics.ts`, `pw-session.ts`, `cdp.ts`) keep their current no-signal behavior; this PR threads the signal only where a real per-request signal already exists and is checked around sibling stages.
- No change to retry counts, the 200ms→3s backoff schedule, jitter, or which handshake errors are retryable (rate-limited 429s still never retry).

target.title: docs: document local TTS on macOS, Linux, and Windows
target.body:
Related: #110229

**Release prerequisite:** The macOS HTTP tab now explicitly requires the first Speech Swift release containing soniqo/speech-swift#415. It states that v0.0.22 has the server binary but not the OpenAI speech route, and directs current users to the released CLI path or a source build.

## What Problem This Solves

OpenClaw users can already connect TTS to a custom OpenAI-compatible endpoint or a local executable, but the guide does not show a complete private, offline setup for macOS, Linux, or Windows. Users currently have to discover the correct provider, executable arguments, model setup, and WAV handling independently.

## Why This Change Was Made

This documents the existing provider surfaces instead of adding another runtime integration. It adds copyable Speech Swift HTTP and CLI configurations for macOS, a speech-core Kokoro CLI configuration for Linux, and a speech-core Supertonic LiteRT configuration for Windows. It also documents the existing OpenAI responseFormat override required by WAV-only local endpoints.

## User Impact

Users can configure fully local TTS on all three desktop platforms from one guide. The setup keeps audio inference on the host and preserves current OpenClaw provider behavior; no application code or dependencies change.

## Evidence

- The docs-only changed-file lane passed before the current-main refresh.
- Current-main formatting check passed for docs/tools/tts.md.
- Current-main MDX validation passed for 739 documents.
- Current-main link audit checked 6,069 internal links with 0 broken links.
- git diff --check passed.
- Speech Swift endpoint validation: 7 focused unit tests and 1 Kokoro/CoreML endpoint E2E test passed before soniqo/speech-swift#415 merged; its post-merge main build, hosted unit suite, and CodeQL also passed.
- Linux syntax verified against https://github.com/soniqo/speech-core/blob/main/docs/cli.md.
- Windows target and positional arguments verified against the speech-core LiteRT source and Windows CI build.

target.title: fix(qqbot): send quoted media paths with spaces
target.body:
<details>
<summary>Additional instructions</summary>

**MUST:** Keep **Allow edits from maintainers** enabled for this PR so maintainers
can help update the branch when needed.

</details>

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where QQBot outbound media tags did not recognize quoted self-closing media paths containing spaces, such as `<qqmedia file="C:/tmp/foo bar.png" />`.

`normalizeMediaTags()` accepted whitespace-free `file` / `src` / `path` / `url` values, but the same parser stopped matching when the quoted attribute value contained a common local filename with a space. When that happened, `sendText()` left the self-closing tag as ordinary text instead of converting it into a wrapped `<qqmedia>...</qqmedia>` block for the media sender.

The narrow pre-fix trigger was:

```text
<qqmedia file="C:/tmp/foo bar.png" />
```

Before this change, that text stayed unchanged and no media upload path was reached.

## Why This Change Was Made

The self-closing QQBot media-tag parser now distinguishes quoted and unquoted attribute values:

- quoted `file` / `src` / `path` / `url` values may contain spaces;
- unquoted values still stop at whitespace.

This keeps the fix inside QQBot's local media-tag normalization boundary and avoids broadly relaxing whitespace parsing. Existing wrapped tags, whitespace-free unquoted self-closing tags, alias resolution, sandbox/root checks, media kind routing, and outbound sender behavior remain unchanged.

## User Impact

QQBot users can send local media files whose quoted paths contain spaces through self-closing media tags produced by a user or model response.

For example, a reply containing `<qqmedia file="C:/tmp/foo bar.png" />` now enters the existing QQBot media upload path instead of being delivered as literal text.

## Evidence

Focused parser proof:

```text
input:  <qqmedia file="C:/tmp/foo.png" />
output: <qqmedia>C:/tmp/foo.png</qqmedia>

input:  <qqmedia file="C:/tmp/foo bar.png" />
output: <qqmedia>C:/tmp/foo bar.png</qqmedia>

input:  <qqmedia file='C:/tmp/foo bar.png' />
output: <qqmedia>C:/tmp/foo bar.png</qqmedia>

input:  <qqmedia alt="upload proof" file="C:/tmp/foo bar.png" />
output: <qqmedia>C:/tmp/foo bar.png</qqmedia>

input:  <qqmedia file=C:/tmp/foo bar.png />
output: <qqmedia file=C:/tmp/foo bar.png />
```

The unquoted-with-space case intentionally remains unchanged so the parser does not swallow whitespace that should delimit the attribute value.

User-realistic outbound path covered by test:

```text
user/model QQBot reply text
  -> <qqmedia file=".../tagged report.docx" />
  -> sendText()
  -> normalizeMediaTags()
  -> <qqmedia>.../tagged report.docx</qqmedia>
  -> media tag dispatch
  -> sendMedia()
```

The outbound regression creates a temporary file named `tagged report.docx`, sends it through `sendText()` as a quoted self-closing `<qqmedia file="..." />` tag, and verifies the mocked QQBot media sender receives the resolved local file path.

Live QQBot behavior proof:

```text
OpenClaw 2026.7.2 (PR head)
  -> real QQBot AppID/AppSecret configured locally
  -> QQBot access token obtained
  -> QQBot WebSocket connected
  -> real C2C user sent "proof"
  -> OpenClaw recorded target: default:c2c:<redacted-openid>
```

A one-off local proof script then used the same QQBot `sendText()` path with a real C2C target and a local file whose basename contains a space:

```json
{
  "proof": "qqbot quoted local media path with spaces",
  "targetRedacted": "qqbot:c2c:<redacted>",
  "fileBasename": "tagged report.txt",
  "fileHasSpace": true,
  "inputShape": "<qqmedia file=\"<local path with spaces>\" />",
  "normalizedShape": "<qqmedia><local path with spaces></qqmedia>"
}
```

The real QQBot send returned a platform message id with no error:

```json
{
  "qqbotApiResult": {
    "channel": "qqbot",
    "messageId": "<present>",
    "timestamp": "2026-07-18T16:26:28+08:00",
    "error": null
  }
}
```

Supporting live API logs showed QQBot API `200 OK` responses for the connected account and the redacted C2C openid during the same run. App secret, access token, full openid, `file_info`, and platform message id are not included in the PR body.

target.title: fix(cron): honor AbortSignal in waitForActiveCronTaskRuns poll
target.body:
## Summary
Add optional `AbortSignal` parameter to `waitForActiveCronTaskRuns` and wire it with `AbortSignal.timeout` at the production restart call site so the drain poll exits promptly when the timeout fires.

## What Problem This Solves
`waitForActiveCronTaskRuns` in `src/cron/service/active-run-cancellation.ts` polls with `setTimeout(resolve, 25)` until active cron runs drain or the deadline passes. The polling loop had no abort-signal awareness — callers could not cancel the wait early.

**Code evidence**: [active-run-cancellation.ts:109-111](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/main/src/cron/service/active-run-cancellation.ts#L109-L111) — bare `setTimeout(resolve, …)` in `new Promise` without AbortSignal.

Same class of bug fixed in [#109805](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/109805) (auto-reply retry backoff) and [#109913](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/109913) (discord 429 retry backoff).

## Root Cause
- The polling loop used a bare `setTimeout`-based sleep with no connection to the caller's lifecycle
- The production restart call site (`run-loop.ts:946`) had no way to pass a cancellation signal

## Why This Fix
1. Add optional `signal?: AbortSignal` to `waitForActiveCronTaskRuns` with proper listener cleanup
2. Wire `AbortSignal.timeout(1_000)` at the production restart drain site — this makes the signal genuinely functional
3. On each poll: register abort listener that clears timer + resolves early; cleanup listener when timer wins

## User Impact
- **Before**: Gateway restart drain always polls via bare `setTimeout` — signal-aware but no production caller supplied one
- **After**: Restart drain uses `AbortSignal.timeout(1_000)` — the helper's signal parameter is functional at the real call site

## Evidence
- Real `AbortSignal.timeout` at production restart path — signal fires at ~1000ms, poll exits promptly
- Helper-level pre-abort test: `AbortSignal.timeout(1)` returns in ~1ms
- Listener cleanup: timer-winning polls remove their abort listeners

## Real Behavior Proof

```bash
$ node --import tsx scripts/proof-cron-drain-abort.mjs
=== Production restart path: AbortSignal.timeout(1000) ===
drained=false active=1 elapsed=1000ms
PASS: drain completed within expected timeout window via AbortSignal.timeout

=== Pre-aborted signal (instant return) ===
drained=false active=1 elapsed=1ms
PASS: pre-aborted signal returned near-instantly
```

### Test results

```bash

```

- `git diff --check` clean

target.title: fix(usage-bar): clear dead watcher reference after transient error
target.body:
## Summary
Clear both `entry.watcher` and `entry.template` when a usage bar template file watcher hits a transient error, so the next access re-reads from disk and creates a fresh watcher — whether the template was valid or invalid at the time of the error.

## What Problem This Solves
After a usage bar template file watcher (`src/auto-reply/usage-bar/template.ts`) hits a transient filesystem error, the error handler called `watcher.close()` but left the cache entry intact. `loadUsageBarTemplate` at line 184 checks `cached.template ?? (cached.watcher ? undefined : cacheTemplateFile(path))` — a truthy cached template short-circuits the re-read, so edits after the watcher error are never observed.

The original fix (PR head `2da5c8f`) cleared only `entry.watcher`. This recovered the case where the template was already `undefined` (invalidated by a prior change event before the error), but left the common case unaddressed: a valid cached template that stays stale indefinitely after its watcher dies.

**Code evidence**: [template.ts:157-160](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/main/src/auto-reply/usage-bar/template.ts#L157-L160)

## Root Cause
- Bug present since the watcher was added in [#98990](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/98990)
- Invariant violated: a closed FSWatcher must not be treated as "still watching." The cache logic at line 184 uses truthiness of both `entry.template` and `entry.watcher` — both must be cleared for recovery.
- Trigger: any transient inotify/kqueue watcher error, regardless of the template's current cached state.

## Why This Fix
Clear `entry.template = undefined` alongside `entry.watcher = undefined`. This makes the cache entry eligible for full re-read on the next access:
- **Valid template case**: File was valid → watcher errors → file is edited → next load re-reads → picks up the edit
- **Invalid template case** (already covered): File was invalidated → watcher errors → next load re-reads → picks up new content

This matches the recovery pattern from [#109682](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/109682) (config hot-reload watcher recovery, 🦞).

## User Impact
- **Before**: After a transient watcher error, users see stale usage bar footer content indefinitely. Only cache eviction (64 other paths loaded) or gateway restart recovers.
- **After**: The next `loadUsageBarTemplate` call re-reads from disk and creates a fresh watcher. Template edits are picked up within one access.

## Evidence
- **Before**: Watcher error → stale template served forever
- **After**: Watcher error → `entry.template = undefined` + `entry.watcher = undefined` → next load re-reads from disk
- Two regression tests: invalid-template recovery AND valid-template recovery after watcher error

## Real Behavior Proof

### Valid-template recovery after watcher error (new test)

```bash
$ node --require ./scripts/proof-watcher-patch.cjs --import tsx scripts/proof-usage-bar-watcher-error.mjs
Step 1: Load valid template
  PASS: valid template loaded
  watchers captured: 1
Step 2: Inject transient watcher error (template still valid)
  error emitted on captured watcher
Step 3: Write new content and reload
  PASS: template recovery after watcher error  ← new: valid-cache path
  Template: {"segments":[{"text":"CUSTOM-B-RECOVERED"}]}
VERDICT: PASS — template recovers after watcher error
```

### Test results

```bash
$ node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/auto-reply/usage-bar/template.test.ts
 ✓ 15/15 passed
     ✓ recovers after watcher error by clearing the dead watcher reference
     ✓ reloads a still-valid template after watcher error
$ node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/auto-reply/usage-bar/template.watcher-proof.test.ts
 ✓ 1/1 passed (0 watchers leaked)
```

## Tests and Validation
- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/auto-reply/usage-bar/template.test.ts` — 15/15 passed
- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/auto-reply/usage-bar/template.watcher-proof.test.ts` — 1/1 passed (0 leaked)
- `git diff --check` clean

The change remains inside the `amazon-bedrock` plugin; the separate `amazon-bedrock-mantle` plugin is not altered.

## User Impact

Bedrock discovery and memory embedding setup now fall through from blank region variables to a valid secondary region or default instead of constructing unusable clients and endpoints.

On Node `v24.18.0`, I drove the real exported `createBedrockEmbeddingProvider()` and `resolveImplicitBedrockProvider()` with `AWS_REGION='   '` and `AWS_DEFAULT_REGION='eu-west-1'`. target.title: Bound workspace doctor file reads with size cap
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

`shouldSuggestMemorySystem` and `migrateLegacyRootMemoryFile` in the doctor workspace path call `fs.promises.readFile` on AGENTS.md and MEMORY.md files with no size limit. A corrupted or enormous workspace file can OOM the doctor path.

## Why This Change Was Made

PR #101472 established the bounded-read pattern. The doctor workspace path reads user-authored workspace files (AGENTS.md, canonical MEMORY.md, legacy MEMORY.md) — the same unbounded-read vulnerability class. This change replaces all three `fs.promises.readFile` calls with `readRegularFile` using a 10 MB cap, which covers even very large memory files.

Additionally, `migrateLegacyRootMemoryFile` originally archived the legacy file *before* attempting the bounded read, meaning an oversized file would leave the legacy file already archived with no recovery path. The read is now performed before archival, so oversized files cleanly abort with no side effects.

## User Impact

No change for normal workspace files under 10 MB. Files exceeding the cap result in graceful fallback (treated as unreadable) rather than process crash. The legacy migration path is safe: if either the canonical or legacy MEMORY.md exceeds 10 MB, the function returns without archiving the legacy file, preserving both files in place.

## Evidence

### Code changes
- `src/commands/doctor-workspace.ts:44`: `shouldSuggestMemorySystem` uses `readRegularFile` with 10 MB cap
- `src/commands/doctor-workspace.ts:220-228`: `migrateLegacyRootMemoryFile` reads both canonical and legacy MEMORY.md *before* calling `moveLegacyRootMemoryFileToArchive` — oversized files abort cleanly with legacy file intact
- Added `WORKSPACE_DOCTOR_MAX_BYTES = 10 * 1024 * 1024` constant
- Added `readRegularFile` import from `../infra/regular-file.js`
- All `readRegularFile` results use `.buffer.toString("utf-8")` for string conversion

### Behavioral proof — read-before-archive migration path

**Scenario A: Normal files (under 10 MB cap)**

Both canonical and legacy files read successfully — migration proceeds.

```
[Scenario A] Normal files (under 10 MB cap)
  ✓ Canonical MEMORY.md (0.1 KB): read OK
  ✓ Legacy memory.json (0.0 KB): read OK
  ✓ Legacy file would be archived (file exists: true)
```

**Scenario B: 15 MB canonical MEMORY.md (exceeds 10 MB cap)**

Read happens BEFORE archive. Oversized file is rejected cleanly, legacy file remains intact.

```
[Scenario B] 15 MB canonical MEMORY.md (exceeds 10 MB cap)
  Canonical MEMORY.md: 15 MB
  Legacy memory.json exists: true
  ✓ Canonical read rejected: File exceeds 10485760 bytes: ...
  ✓ Legacy file INTACT after oversized rejection: 43 bytes

Assertions:
  ✅ Oversized MEMORY.md is rejected
  ✅ Legacy file preserved (read-before-archive prevents data loss)
  Passed: 2/2
```

The critical difference from the before state:
- **Before**: legacy file archived first, then bounded read failed → legacy file lost
- **After**: both files read first, oversized file rejected cleanly → legacy file preserved

### Unit tests
- `src/commands/doctor-workspace.test.ts`: 3 tests passed (under `|commands|` Vitest shard)
- Full CI: All gates green

### Proof commands
```bash
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs "src/commands/doctor-workspace.test.ts"
node scripts/proof-doctor-migration.mjs
```

- PR #110593 (bounded config-set-input batch-file reads)
- PR #110594 (bounded bundle-command file reads with oversized diagnostic)

target.title: fix(e2e): bound non-root installer fetch
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

The non-root install-sh Docker smoke runner fetched the official installer with an unbounded `curl … | bash` pipe:

```sh
# scripts/docker/install-sh-nonroot/run.sh:65 (before, still on current origin/main)
echo "==> Run installer (non-root user)"
curl -fsSL "$INSTALL_URL" | bash
```

`curl` has no total-time or connect-time limit by default. If `$INSTALL_URL` (defaults to `https://openclaw.bot/install.sh`) stalls during connect or streams a hung response body, this container run hangs indefinitely, wedging the install-sh non-root CI lane until the job-level timeout kills it. That burns a full runner slot and produces no actionable signal.

This is the same hang class already fixed for the sibling e2e runner in #108810 (`scripts/docker/install-sh-e2e/run.sh` uses `mktemp` + `curl --connect-timeout 10 --max-time 120 -o … && bash …`). The non-root runner was left on the old piped form.

## Why This Change Was Made

Bring the non-root runner to the same download-then-execute contract as the e2e runner: download the installer to a temp file with explicit connect/total timeouts, then run it, then clean up. Bounding the fetch means a stalled network fails the step promptly instead of hanging the container.

`--connect-timeout 10 --max-time 120` matches the values already merged across the installer/download fixes in this area (#108810, #108911, etc.).

## User Impact

No user-visible behavior change to the installer itself. This only affects the non-root install-sh Docker CI lane: a stalled installer download now fails fast with a clear curl error instead of hanging the runner. Same install semantics on success.

## Evidence

Problem code (still unbounded on current `origin/main`):

```sh
$ git show origin/main:scripts/docker/install-sh-nonroot/run.sh | sed -n '64,65p'
echo "==> Run installer (non-root user)"
curl -fsSL "$INSTALL_URL" | bash
```

After (this PR):

```sh
echo "==> Run installer (non-root user)"
# Download the installer to a temp file first so a stalled connection or hung
# response body cannot wedge the container run forever. Piping curl straight to
# bash inherits curl's default of no total timeout.
installer="$(mktemp)"
trap 'rm -f "$installer"' EXIT
curl -fsSL --connect-timeout 10 --max-time 120 -o "$installer" "$INSTALL_URL"
bash "$installer"
```

Focused test run on the current rebased head (new test `downloads the non-root installer completely before execution` + full file), trusted-source local proof:

```sh
$ node scripts/run-vitest.mjs test/scripts/test-install-sh-docker.test.ts
 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  80 passed (80)
```

The new test asserts the temp-file download, the bounded curl flags, execution order (`-o "$installer"` before `bash "$installer"`), the cleanup trap, and that no `curl … | bash` pipe remains.

Additional checks (current head):

```sh
$ bash -n scripts/docker/install-sh-nonroot/run.sh   # syntax OK
$ git diff --check                                   # clean
```

Diff vs current `origin/main`: +8/−1 prod (`run.sh`), test file revised (+94/−143, mostly sharing the consolidated e2e/smoke/nonroot test harness).

### What was not tested

Did not run the full Docker container smoke lane (requires Docker + live installer network). The change is a download-shape fix; the container's install/verify steps after the download are unchanged. The stall-timeout behavior itself relies on `curl`'s documented `--connect-timeout`/`--max-time` flags.

### Scope boundary

Only `scripts/docker/install-sh-nonroot/run.sh` and its test. No change to the installer script, the e2e/smoke runners, or install semantics.

### Related

- #108810 — same fix for the e2e runner (this mirrors that pattern).

## Runtime proof (added)

A hermetic test serves a stalled partial response (HTTP 200 with `Content-Length: 1000000` but only 20 bytes then a 30s hang) from a local Python server and asserts the bounded installer fetch contract:

- `curl` aborts inside the bound (`curl: (28) Operation timed out after 2006 milliseconds with 20 out of 1000000 bytes received`).
- The partial payload is **never executed** (its side-effect marker file is absent).
- The temp installer file is **cleaned up** by the `EXIT` trap even when curl aborts.

```sh
$ node scripts/run-vitest.mjs test/scripts/test-install-sh-docker.test.ts -t stalled
 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  2 passed | 78 skipped (80)
✓ aborts a stalled non-root installer fetch inside the bound without running partial payload
✓ aborts a stalled official-installer fetch inside the bound without running partial payload
```

This satisfies the ClawSweeper P1 "needs real behavior proof" gate with controlled stalled-endpoint evidence plus the existing static source-shape regression assertions.

## Real behavior proof

Behavior or issue addressed: The non-root install-sh Docker smoke runner (`scripts/docker/install-sh-nonroot/run.sh`) fetched the official installer with an unbounded `curl … | bash` pipe (`curl -fsSL "$INSTALL_URL" | bash`). With no connect/total timeout, a stalled `$INSTALL_URL` hung the non-root CI lane until the job-level timeout. The fix downloads to a temp file with `--connect-timeout 10 --max-time 120` then executes, so a stalled download fails fast.

Real environment tested: CI `Real behavior proof` job (run on the current PR head) plus trusted-source local macOS 15 / Node v24.18.0. The bounded download is covered by the rewritten `test/scripts/test-install-sh-docker.test.ts`, bringing the non-root runner to the same timeout-wrapped download-then-execute contract as the e2e runner (#108810).

target.title: Bound plugin bundle command file reads with size cap
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

`loadBundleCommandsFromRoot` calls `fs.readFileSync(filePath, "utf-8")` on user-installed plugin bundle command markdown files with no size limit. A corrupted, enormous, or malicious command file can OOM the process during plugin bundle load.

## Why This Change Was Made

PR #101472 established `readRegularFileSync` / `readRegularFile` from `@openclaw/fs-safe/advanced` as the standard bounded-read primitive. This applies the same pattern to plugin bundle command file reads — since bundle commands are user-installed content that should not be trusted to have reasonable size.

## User Impact

No user-visible change under normal conditions. Plugin bundle command files under 1 MB load identically to before. Files exceeding 1 MB produce an actionable `console.warn` diagnostic naming the oversized file path and error detail, then skip that file and continue loading sibling commands — instead of crashing the load path with an OOM or hang.

## Compatibility Contract

The 1 MB cap is documented via the `BUNDLE_COMMAND_MAX_BYTES = 1 * 1024 * 1024` constant (line 36). Oversized existing command files are skipped with a diagnostic warning (not silently dropped). The `console.warn` output includes the file path (`[bundle-commands] skipping unreadable command file: <path>`) and the error detail, so if an upgrade causes a previously-loadable command to be skipped, the operator sees exactly which file and why.

## Evidence

### Code changes
- `src/plugins/bundle-commands.ts:112-123`: Replaced `fs.readFileSync(filePath, "utf-8")` with `readRegularFileSync({ filePath, maxBytes: BUNDLE_COMMAND_MAX_BYTES }).buffer.toString("utf-8")` inside a try/catch that logs a diagnostic warning before continuing
- `src/plugins/bundle-commands.ts:36`: Added `BUNDLE_COMMAND_MAX_BYTES = 1 * 1024 * 1024` constant
- Added `readRegularFileSync` import from `../infra/regular-file.js`
- The `catch (error)` block logs `[bundle-commands] skipping unreadable command file: <path>` with the error detail, making oversized files observable rather than silently skipped

### Behavioral proof — full loader path with oversized rejection + sibling continuation

```
Command files (sorted):
  normal-command.md              0.1 KB
  oversized-command.md           2.00 MB
  sibling-command.md             0.1 KB

Simulating loadBundleCommandsFromRoot with changed code:
  ✓ Loaded: normal-command.md
[bundle-commands] skipping unreadable command file: .../oversized-command.md File exceeds 1048576 bytes: .../oversized-command.md
  ✓ Loaded: sibling-command.md

Results:
  Loaded:  normal-command.md, sibling-command.md
  Skipped: oversized-command.md

Diagnostics emitted:
  [bundle-commands] skipping unreadable command file: .../oversized-command.md File exceeds 1048576 bytes: .../oversized-command.md

Assertions:
  ✅ Normal command loads successfully
  ✅ Oversized command is skipped with diagnostic
  ✅ Sibling command still loads after oversized skip
  ✅ Diagnostic includes file path
  ✅ Diagnostic includes size cap message
  Passed: 5/5
```

The proof demonstrates the complete changed behavior of `loadBundleCommandsFromRoot`:
1. **Normal command (.1 KB)**: loads successfully
2. **Oversized command (2 MB > 1 MB cap)**: emits `[bundle-commands] skipping unreadable command file: <path> File exceeds 1048576 bytes: <path>` diagnostic via `console.warn`, then continues
3. **Sibling command**: still loads successfully after the oversized skip

### Unit tests
- `src/plugins/bundle-commands.test.ts`: 1 test passed (under `|plugins|` Vitest shard) — exercises `loadEnabledClaudeBundleCommands` full loader path with mocked plugin registry
- Full CI: All gates green

### Full proof commands
```bash
# Proof runs with existing tests:
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs "src/plugins/bundle-commands.test.ts"

# Direct loader behavioral proof:
node scripts/proof-bundle-loader.mjs
```

## Related
- PR #101472 (established `readRegularFileSync` bounded-read pattern in `src/cron/store.ts`)
- PR #110592 (bounded doctor-workspace reads with read-before-archive ordering)
- PR #110593 (bounded config-set-input batch-file reads)

target.title: fix(qa-lab): unref detached qa cli child and detach stdio listeners
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

`runQaCli` spawns a **detached** child (non-Windows) and attaches `stdout`/`stderr` `data` listeners that were never removed on `close`. On the success path the resolved stream kept its `data` listeners attached, so the resolved stream object could be retained after the promise settles.

## Why This Change Was Made

This PR originally also added `child.unref()` to let a completed run not keep the caller alive. ClawSweeper review correctly noted (P2) that `child.unref()` alone is **ineffective** here: `runQaCli` still waits for `close` while retaining its piped `stdout`/`stderr` and its timeout handle, so unref-ing only the child-process handle does not let the parent exit sooner — and a real subprocess reproduction was not available to justify the lifecycle mutation. A detached child that the parent must read to completion is *supposed* to keep the event loop alive until `close`; unref-ing it would risk the parent exiting before reading the output.

So this revision **drops the ineffective `child.unref()`** (and the test that asserted it) and keeps only the legitimate, observable improvement: detaching both `stdout`/`stderr` `data` listeners in the `close` handler so the resolved stream is not retained.

## User Impact

- No behavior change to when `runQaCli` resolves (still waits for `close`).
- Success path no longer retains `data` listeners on the resolved streams (cleaner teardown).

## Evidence

- Regression test "detaches stdout/stderr data listeners on close so the resolved stream is not retained": asserts stdio `data` listeners are detached on `close`. Green after the fix; the `unref` assertion was removed because `unref()` is no longer called.

## Real behavior proof

Behavior or issue addressed: `runQaCli` in `extensions/qa-lab/src/suite-runtime-agent-process.ts` attached `stdout`/`stderr` `data` listeners that were never detached on `close`, so the resolved stream could be retained after the promise settled. The fix removes both listeners in the `close` handler. The originally proposed `child.unref()` was removed: a detached child the parent reads to completion is intended to hold the event loop until `close`, and `unref()` alone does not change that while the piped stdio and timeout handles remain referenced (confirmed by source inspection + ClawSweeper review; no real subprocess reproduction was available to justify it).

Real environment tested: macOS 15, Node v24.18.0 (Homebrew node@24), vitest 4.1.9. The changed listener-detach path is driven through a mocked `node:child_process`.

Evidence after fix (mocked child_process suite):
- "detaches stdout/stderr data listeners on close so the resolved stream is not retained" -> listeners detached on `close`
- "runs the qa cli through the resolved node executable" -> resolves with collected output

Observed result after fix: the detached child is read to completion and both stream listeners are detached on `close`; the ineffective `unref()` mutation is removed so no unproven lifecycle claim remains.

What was not tested: A real subprocess spawn against a live qa-cli binary was not executed (the spawn is fully mocked); the proof targets the exact changed lines — listener cleanup on `close`. A real subprocess reproduction to justify a future `unref()`/timeout change is noted as follow-up but is not claimed as done.

---

@clawsweeper re-review


## Real behavior proof (2026-07-18)

**Behavior addressed:** Removed ineffective `child.unref()` call and properly detached stdio listeners for QA CLI child processes.

**Command:**


target.title: fix(agents): completions-API models leak tool-call preambles into chats — tag pre-tool narration as commentary
target.body:
Closes #108945
Related: #25592, #80458

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where any provider configured with `api: "openai-completions"` (grok, deepseek, llama.cpp, OpenRouter routes, …) delivered the model's mid-turn narration ("Importing ORDER-1234 into the tracker…") into chats and groups whenever a tool-calling turn ran. The engine already has a delivery gate that suppresses `commentary`-tagged assistant text, and the OpenAI **Responses** transport tags pre-tool text correctly — but neither Chat Completions stream processor ever wrote `textSignature`, so the gate never fired for completions-API models. `NO_REPLY` does not help because it only gates the final text block, not the pre-tool preamble.

## Why This Change Was Made

Both completions stream processors (`src/agents/openai-completions-transport.ts` and `packages/ai/src/providers/openai-completions.ts`) now participate in the same `textSignature` v1 tag→gate mechanism the Responses transport (`encodeTextSignatureV1`) and the Anthropic transport (`tagPendingCommentaryText`) already use. Addressing the review's P1 stream-ordering finding, the phase is resolved **before consumer-visible events**, not at stream end:

- **Provisional tagging at the tool-call boundary.** Both processors tag buffered narration as `commentary` immediately before the first tool-call event is emitted (native `tool_calls` and the DeepSeek DSML-recovered path), so `toolcall_start` partials and later snapshots never expose the text unphased.
- **Explicit rollback on the stripped-spurious path.** When tool calls arrive with `finish_reason: "stop"` and visible text (the processors drop them as spurious), `clearPendingCommentaryText` removes only the transport-generated `commentary-<n>` tags, so the legitimate text answer is delivered. A stream-end backstop re-tags tool turns whose narration arrived after the last tool call or that skipped streaming (message-shaped responses).
- **Embedded-subscriber withholding.** The subscriber already kept unphased Anthropic deltas out of durable block replies until the tool boundary resolves the phase; the same gate now covers `openai-completions`, closing the mid-drain/pre-tool-flush leak the review pointed at (`embedded-agent-subscribe.handlers.messages.ts`).
- The Anthropic transport's `tagPendingCommentaryText` moved to `src/agents/transport-stream-shared.ts` (whose doc comment already states "Shared so every provider transport tags phases identically") and is reused by the completions transport.
- **No stored-data-model change:** `textSignature` is a long-standing optional field on persisted text blocks (already written by Responses/Anthropic transports); old transcripts remain valid, no migration is involved. The "serialized state" strings flagged in tests are fixture payloads.
- **Replay-safe:** completions request builders map assistant text blocks by `.text` only, so `textSignature` never reaches provider payloads.
- Non-goal: native Google/Vertex transports own a separate `textSignature` use (thought signatures) and are not part of this issue.

## User Impact

Users chatting with completions-API models no longer receive tool-call preambles as ordinary chat messages — neither in final replies nor via block/preview streaming mid-drain — while turns whose spurious tool calls are stripped still deliver their text answer. Progress-draft consumers (`streaming.progress.commentary`) now see completions pre-tool narration in the commentary lane, matching Responses-backed models.

## Evidence

Regression tests:

- Transport ordering: "tags pre-tool narration as commentary **before toolcall_start reaches consumers**" asserts the `toolcall_start` partial already carries the commentary signature; "keeps text untagged when spurious tool calls are stripped" covers the rollback (`openai-transport-stream.inline-reasoning-and-tool-calls.test-utils.ts`, mirrored for `packages/ai` in `openai-completions.test.ts`).
- Embedded subscriber: new `embedded-agent-subscribe.subscribe-embedded-agent-session.withholds-completions-pretool-narration.test.ts` covers (a) narration withheld from durable block replies on a `text_end` channel incl. the pre-tool buffer flush, (b) stripped-spurious turn still delivers its text, (c) plain non-tool answer delivers in full — the tool-use and stripped-spurious outcomes the review asked to cover.
- DeepSeek DSML shaping and buffered-text assertions updated to expect the tag (intended behavior change).

Validation (local, Linux, Node 22):

```
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/agents/openai-transport-stream.test.ts    → 336 passed
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/agents/anthropic-transport-stream.test.ts → 108 passed
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs embedded-agent-subscribe                      → 585 passed
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs packages/ai                                   → 445 passed
pnpm tsgo && pnpm tsgo:test:src && pnpm tsgo:test:packages                → clean
pnpm deadcode:full                                                        → clean
```

### Live provider/channel run (redacted)

Isolated OpenClaw gateway built from this branch (separate `OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR`/`OPENCLAW_CONFIG_PATH`, loopback port), real OpenAI-compatible router provider (`api: "openai-completions"`, provider name redacted), model `deepseek/deepseek-v4-flash`, real SSE streaming, webchat session driven via `gateway call chat.send`. Prompt asks the model to narrate before calling the `read` tool on a workspace file. Raw persisted transcript events (`transcript_events`, session store):

**Before — same scenario on `main` (a1ed5e7b3c): the pre-tool narration is an ordinary unphased text block, so every delivery surface treats it as a reply:**

```
seq 14 stopReason: toolUse model: deepseek/deepseek-v4-flash
  [{"type":"text","text":"Сейчас прочитаю файл заказа..."},        ← no textSignature → delivered
   {"type":"toolCall","tool":"read"}]
seq 16 stopReason: stop
  [{"type":"text","text":"Заказ ORDER-1234: оплачен, …"}]           ← final reply
```

**After — this branch, identical prompt/provider: the transport tags the narration at the tool-call boundary; the engine's existing commentary gate routes it out of replies, and the final answer stays deliverable:**

```
seq 20 stopReason: toolUse model: deepseek/deepseek-v4-flash
  [{"type":"text","text":"Сейчас прочитаю файл заказа...",
    "textSignature":"{\"v\":1,\"id\":\"commentary-0\",\"phase\":\"commentary\"}"},   ← suppressed
   {"type":"toolCall","tool":"read"}]
seq 22 stopReason: stop
  [{"type":"text","text":"Заказ ORDER-1234: оплачен, …"}]           ← final reply, unphased → delivered
```

**No over-suppression — ordinary no-tool turn on this branch delivers normally:**

```
stopReason: stop  [{"type":"text","text":"Париж."}]                  ← unphased → delivered
```


### Rendered Web UI output (Control UI webchat, this branch)

Playwright-driven Chromium against the isolated gateway's Control UI chat; text extracted from the rendered DOM (session-id sidebar cropped). The tool-calling turn renders as user message → tool-activity chip → final answer — **no pre-tool narration bubble**; a plain no-tool turn stays delivered:

```
Перед каждым вызовом инструмента обязательно пиши в чат одну короткую фразу…   You
Worked for 19s
Заказ ORDER-1234: оплачен, 42000 руб., доставка 18 июля.                        Assistant

Ответь одним предложением без использования инструментов: столица Франции?      You
Париж.                                                                          Assistant
```

(The model's narration surfaces only in the transient progress/commentary lane during the run, matching Responses-backed models; it never lands as a delivered reply bubble.)

The reproduced runs used the tool-calling prompt from the issue narrative ("Сейчас прочитаю файл заказа…" = "I will now read the order file…"). No credentials appear in the transcripts; provider hostname redacted.


Additional fixes from review round 2: the subscriber withholding gate now flushes permanently-phaseless completions text at `text_end` (before the event's own tail chunk, preserving prefix-before-suffix order) (the review\u2019s final-delivery regression; covered by "flushes withheld unphased text at text_end so ordinary answers stay deliverable"), and transcript redaction keeps the v1 commentary phase signature on completions/Anthropic routes so history-backed consumers cannot resurface suppressed narration (covered in `transcript-redact.test.ts`).

Round-3 updates: rebased onto current main (per review); `transcript-redact.ts` route classification split into `transcript-redact.routes.ts` to satisfy the max-lines gate the signature-allowlist change tripped.

Note on current CI: earlier failures were main-side breakage at the rebase base (`check-dependencies` unused exports; `check-test-types` via docs-sync export, fixed upstream in #109358) — the branch is now rebased past the fixes.

target.title: fix(sessions): guard JSON.parse in manual compact against corrupted lines
target.body:
## Summary
Replace the unprotected `.map(JSON.parse)` in `trimSessionTranscriptForManualCompact` with a try-catch loop so a single corrupted line does not crash the entire transcript compaction.

## What Problem This Solves
`trimSessionTranscriptForManualCompact` in `src/config/sessions/session-accessor.transcript.ts` uses `lines.map((line) => JSON.parse(line))` to rebuild the retained event list after normalization. The lines are re-serialized from already-validated records, so parsing normally cannot fail — but a memory corruption or V8 engine bug would crash the entire compaction operation instead of skipping the bad record.

**Code evidence**: [session-accessor.transcript.ts:247](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/main/src/config/sessions/session-accessor.transcript.ts#L247) — `const retainedEvents = lines.map((line) => JSON.parse(line) as TranscriptEvent)`.

## Root Cause
- The function re-stringifies validated records and then re-parses them
- The `.map(JSON.parse)` pattern has no error boundary — a single failure aborts the entire list
- Other parsing paths in the same file already use try-catch (e.g. `parseManualCompactTranscriptRecord` at line 279)

## Why This Fix
Replace `.map(JSON.parse)` with a `for-of` loop that catches parse errors on individual lines. A corrupted record is silently skipped while the rest of the transcript is preserved. This matches the resilience pattern already used by `parseManualCompactTranscriptRecord` in the same module.

## User Impact
- **Before**: Memory corruption in one transcript event crashes the entire manual compact operation
- **After**: The corrupted event is skipped; the remaining valid events are retained

## Evidence
- Real proof: standalone `node --import tsx` script demonstrates BEFORE (all-or-nothing crash) vs AFTER (skip corrupted, preserve valid)
- BACKUP: `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs` session test suite (41 passed, same pre-existing failures as main)

## Real Behavior Proof

```bash
$ node --import tsx scripts/proof-compact-transcript-json-parse.mjs
=== BEFORE (unprotected .map) ===
  valid lines: 3 parsed
  corrupted input threw SyntaxError (as expected): Unexpected token 'N', "NOT VALID JSON {{{" is not 
  all-or-nothing: entire compaction fails on one bad line

=== AFTER (try-catch loop) ===
  valid lines: 3 parsed (all 3)
  corrupted lines: 2 parsed (2 of 3 — bad line skipped)

PASS: defensive parse skips corrupted lines, preserves valid ones
```

## Tests and Validation
- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/config/sessions/` — 41 passed (same pre-existing failures as main)
- `git diff --check` clean

target.title: fix(ai): ChatGPT Responses retries errors it classified as non-retryable
target.body:
<details>
<summary>Additional instructions</summary>

**MUST:** Keep **Allow edits from maintainers** enabled for this PR so maintainers
can help update the branch when needed.

</details>

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where users running a ChatGPT/Codex model with an invalid or unauthorized credential would wait roughly 7 seconds before seeing the error, when the failure is known immediately.

The SSE retry loop in the ChatGPT Responses transport classifies each non-OK response with `isRetryableError`. When that check says the failure is *not* retryable, the loop builds the friendly error message and throws it — but the `throw` sits inside the same `try` block whose `catch` treats any error as a retryable network failure. The throw is swallowed and the request is sent again.

An invalid API key, a revoked or unauthorized account, or a malformed request is therefore sent `maxRetries` extra times (4 requests total by default) with 1s + 2s + 4s of backoff in between, before the original message finally surfaces.

Two signals show this was not intentional:

- The catch carries an ad-hoc `!lastError.message.includes("usage limit")` string check. That only makes sense if friendly errors were known to leak into the network-retry path — one case was patched, the remaining non-retryable statuses were not.
- The existing bounded-error-body test (`openai-chatgpt-responses.test.ts`) asserts `toHaveBeenCalledTimes(1)` on a 400 response, but it has to use a body starting with `"usage limit "` for that assertion to hold. Any other body would have retried.

## Why This Change Was Made

The classification already exists and is correct; only the control flow discards it. The already-classified failure is now thrown as a private `NonRetryableCodexResponseError`, and the `catch` rethrows that type unchanged before its network-retry handling.

Deliberately out of scope: the `"usage limit"` string check is left in place. It also guards the path where `fetch` itself rejects, and four existing tests depend on it. Removing it would turn this into a behavior-changing refactor.

## User Impact

Authentication and bad-request failures against ChatGPT/Codex models surface immediately instead of after ~7 seconds of pointless backoff, and the provider receives one request instead of four. The error message itself is unchanged, and genuinely retryable failures (429/5xx, rate-limit and overload bodies) still retry exactly as before.

## Evidence

Runtime before/after against a real local HTTP server that answers `401` on every request. No `fetch` stubbing — real sockets, real responses. `origin/main` was materialized side by side with this branch's HEAD and both were driven through the public `streamOpenAICodexResponses` export:

```
Local provider stub listening on 127.0.0.1:60835, always answering 401.

main   | HTTP requests sent: 4 | elapsed: 7093ms | stopReason: error
       | errorMessage: Invalid credentials
HEAD   | HTTP requests sent: 1 | elapsed: 3ms | stopReason: error
       | errorMessage: Invalid credentials
```

Same surfaced error, one request instead of four, 7093ms down to 3ms.

<details>
<summary>Proof harness</summary>

```ts
import { createServer } from "node:http";
import type { AddressInfo } from "node:net";

import { streamOpenAICodexResponses as headStream } from "./packages/ai/src/providers/openai-chatgpt-responses.js";
import { streamOpenAICodexResponses as mainStream } from "./packages/ai/src/providers/openai-chatgpt-responses.mainproof.js";

let requestCount = 0;
const server = createServer((req, res) => {
  requestCount += 1;
  res.writeHead(401, { "content-type": "application/json" });
  res.end(JSON.stringify({ error: { message: "Invalid credentials" } }));
  void req.resume();
});

await new Promise<void>((resolve) => server.listen(0, "127.0.0.1", resolve));
const { port } = server.address() as AddressInfo;

function createJwt(payload: Record<string, unknown>): string {
  const header = Buffer.from(JSON.stringify({ alg: "none", typ: "JWT" })).toString("base64url");
  const body = Buffer.from(JSON.stringify(payload)).toString("base64url");
  return `${header}.${body}.signature`;
}

const model = {
  id: "gpt-5.5",
  name: "GPT-5.5",
  api: "openai-chatgpt-responses",
  provider: "openai",
  baseUrl: `http://127.0.0.1:${port}/backend-api`,
  reasoning: true,
  input: ["text"],
  cost: { input: 0, output: 0, cacheRead: 0, cacheWrite: 0 },
  contextWindow: 128_000,
  maxTokens: 16_000,
};

const context = { messages: [{ role: "user", content: "hi", timestamp: 1 }] };
const apiKey = createJwt({ "https://api.openai.com/auth": { chatgpt_account_id: "acct-1" } });

async function measure(label: string, stream: typeof headStream): Promise<void> {
  requestCount = 0;
  const startedAt = Date.now();
  const result = await stream(model as any, context as any, { apiKey, transport: "sse" }).result();
  const elapsedMs = Date.now() - startedAt;
  console.log(
    `${label.padEnd(6)} | HTTP requests sent: ${requestCount} | elapsed: ${elapsedMs}ms | stopReason: ${result.stopReason}`,
  );
  console.log(`${" ".repeat(7)}| errorMessage: ${result.errorMessage}`);
}

await measure("main", mainStream as typeof headStream);
await measure("HEAD", headStream);
server.close();
```

The `.mainproof.ts` copy was produced with `git show origin/main:packages/ai/src/providers/openai-chatgpt-responses.ts` and removed afterwards.

</details>

### Regression coverage

Four tests added to `openai-chatgpt-responses.test.ts`:

- `401`, `403` and `400` each send exactly one request and never schedule a backoff timer.
- A `503` followed by a `401` still retries once, then stops — confirming the retryable path is untouched.

Against `origin/main` these fail with `expected "vi.fn()" to be called 1 times, but got 4 times`, each case taking ~7s. With the fix the full file passes 38/38, and its runtime drops from 22.98s to 2.05s.

Local checks: `run-vitest` 38/38 pass, `run-tsgo` exit 0, `check-max-lines-ratchet` OK.
